## Design

### 2026-10-11 – Making the schematic was pretty straightforward, but laying out the pcb took me a while because I had to learn about where to place mounting screws on a pcb, and not to leave empty vias everywhere. I

**4h**

Making the schematic was pretty straightforward, but laying out the pcb took me a while because I had to learn about where to place mounting screws on a pcb, and not to leave empty vias everywhere. I also improved the efficiency of my pcb trace routing, in previous projects I’ve done, I have been more focused on just getting everything connected than on making it compact and reusing sections of copper tracing whenever possible. I also decided to add a place on my pcb where I could attach a plantower pms5003 I used in a previous project that was just built around the sensor and an arduino uno on a breadboard. Next session I’ll work on the software/firmware components.
ps. I forgot to take photos along the way so here are photos of my pcb layout, my schematic layout, and my breadboard project that inspired me to add the pms5003 to this project(more so the remains of it, it was sitting in my parts bin for a while.)
pps. I know it’s a bit unrelated, but I also attached a photo of the m6600 I just finished repairing that I’ll hopefully use for kicad in the future (as soon as I can find a proper 240w charger for it instead of the 130w one I’m using now that gives an unusable framerate in kicad because of how much the cpu gets throttled.(the problem with the laptop I used for this project, is it is a school device and as such I can’t record the screen for timelapses, so images are all for now.)

### 2026-10-11 – ![Screenshot 2026-10-11 at 10.05.07 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/7A0enbFfHqbR9zBP3baSA557supJNoa6/04fbcd545450cad015455f20b986e4d6c5222a1a7843483d91aeed84454245

**2h**

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 at 10.05.07 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/7A0enbFfHqbR9zBP3baSA557supJNoa6/04fbcd545450cad015455f20b986e4d6c5222a1a7843483d91aeed8445424583.png)

I edited the initial firmware file slightly and installed all the necessary library's for the board, I wish I had started writing the firmware earlier in the week so I could have worked on the ui for all the sensors.
Apparently I somehow forgot that the 1x8 connector was representing the mpu6050, so whoops, I guess I'll end up doing some extra soldering to fix that.
Everything else seems right though, so as long as I dont shake it too hard it should stay together,( I'm planning on making a case for it anyways using the m3 screw mounts I added to the pcb)
It takes me a lot longer to write the firmware than to actually make the board layout, even though the arduino language is somewhat similar to the Java that I'm used to, I had to keep looking up what different keywords did. There were so many different void classes in the example code and it was a little overwhelming. I think in the future I'll stick to cad and pcb design.
I also learned that defining sprites for the oled display is pretty similar to making svgs for web design, so I will probably edit the sprite in the future(tomorrow maybe? I have a day off).
Everytime I compile sketches it makes me grateful that java compiles so fast.

Since this initial sketch only uses 26% of program memory(Way larger than my arduino uno), I might leave it in while I add more menus and features to the firmware to support some of the hardware additions I made.

I also spent some time looking up where to get all my necessary bom components at the lowest prices possible. And making my readme and repository look a bit more presentable.

I ended up compiling and uploading all of my gerber files to the repository in this session as well.
